fluff.overview:
The Inquisitor is a 35-ton SecurityMech introduced in 3062 by Irian Technologies, Unlimited, designed exclusively to defend the megacorporation's extensive network of factories and industrial complexes across the Free Worlds League. Built to IndustrialMech specifications but armed and armored to standards that push the legal boundaries of recognized treaties, the Inquisitor has earned a reputation as the closest thing to a true BattleMech in the SecurityMech class.

Originally restricted to internal use by IrTech, the design was released to the open market following the Jihad. Aggressive pricing and strong performance reviews propelled the Inquisitor to become one of the most recognizable and widespread SecurityMechs in the Inner Sphere, frequently mentioned alongside the Copper, Guard, and Pacifier as a benchmark of the class.
fluff.capabilities:
The Inquisitor's weapons loadout positions it at the very edge of what interstellar law permits for a SecurityMech. A Diverse Optics extended range medium laser provides accurate fire at medium ranges, while an Irian Weapon Works Class 4 SRM launcher delivers credible anti-armor punch at closer distances. Twin Voelkers 200 machine guns round out the armament, offering effective suppression against unarmored infantry and rioters. All weapons are managed through an advanced fire control system, granting accuracy comparable to dedicated military platforms.

The ITW Heavy Industrial chassis carries seven tons of Irian HardCase heavy industrial armor, providing protection that rivals some light BattleMechs. An ITW 175 fusion engine propels the design to a respectable 86 kilometers per hour, giving it the mobility to patrol large industrial complexes or respond rapidly to perimeter breaches. Two tons of dedicated communications equipment via the McCall Home-10 CommoRig allow the pilot to coordinate effectively with other security assets and local law enforcement.

The design's primary weakness is its lack of CASE protection for its ammunition stores. The unprotected right torso earned the ITW-80 a poor reputation among pilots for its tendency toward catastrophic ammunition explosions, a flaw that would not be addressed until the introduction of the ITW-85 variant decades later. An ejection seat provides the pilot a last resort should the armor be breached.
fluff.history:
The Inquisitor was born from Irian Technologies' need for a capable in-house security platform during the technological watershed years following the Clan Invasion. Introduced in 3062, the design was initially deployed exclusively to protect IrTech's factories, research facilities, and industrial complexes throughout the Free Worlds League. The timing of its introduction, coinciding with rising tensions that would soon erupt into the FedCom Civil War, proved fortuitous as corporate security concerns across the Inner Sphere reached new heights.

The Word of Blake Jihad transformed the Inquisitor from a corporate security tool into a widespread combat asset. When the Blakists seized control of Irian, they gained access to a steady supply of Inquisitors and deployed them extensively to guard their factories, industrial complexes, and Protectorate installations. TerraSec, the Word of Blake's security apparatus, became one of the design's most prolific operators. By the time of Operation SCOUR, the Inquisitor was among the most common SecurityMechs in TerraSec's ranks. Although individual Inquisitors posed little threat to the dedicated warriors of Stone's coalition forces, their sheer numbers made many liberation engagements considerably more difficult than anticipated. Few TerraSec Inquisitors survived the final battles for Terra.

The post-Jihad period saw the Inquisitor's greatest proliferation. Legal maneuvering against Devlin Stone's fledgling Republic government allowed IrTech to reestablish operations on Terra, while other Terran manufacturers pursued compensation and engaged in work stoppages. Many local police forces, particularly in Europe, turned to salvaged and refurbished Inquisitors to rebuild their security capabilities. IrTech capitalized on this demand by pushing aggressively lower prices throughout the Republic, and the ITW-80 quickly became a familiar sight. Favorable reviews in security trade publications helped drive foreign sales, and by the mid-thirty-first century the Inquisitor had achieved status as one of the most recognizable SecurityMechs in the Inner Sphere.

The design's legacy continued into the Dark Age, with Irian Technologies introducing the ITW-85 variant in the 3120s and the heavier Inquisitor II to meet evolving security demands. Through political upheaval, factory seizures, and shifting national borders, the Inquisitor has remained a constant presence in facility security operations across the Inner Sphere.
fluff.deployment: Introduced in the 3120s, the ITW-85 is the only variant of the Inquisitor authorized by Irian Technologies. Drawing on improved components originally developed for the heavier Inquisitor II, this variant replaces the ITW-80's dedicated communications equipment with a Beagle active probe and improved CASE II protection. The addition of the active probe significantly enhances the ITW-85's ability to detect concealed threats and hidden intruders, while CASE II addresses the original design's most criticized vulnerability by protecting the pilot from catastrophic ammunition detonation. These changes shift the ITW-85 toward a dedicated picket and perimeter security role similar to that of the ITW-200 Inquisitor II, albeit in a lighter and more affordable package.
